title: GOD HAS UNCOVERED YOUR SERVANTS' GUILT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'What can we say to my lord?' Judah replied. 'What can we say? How can we prove our innocence? God has uncovered your servants' guilt. We are now my lord's slaves—we ourselves and the one who was found to have the cup.'" — Gen 44:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is the turning point of the entire chapter, and it comes out of Judah's mouth.

Notice what he does not say. He does not say "we stole the cup" — because they did not. He does not protest their innocence either, though he easily could. Instead he says something far deeper: "God has uncovered your servants' guilt."

Judah has stopped talking about the cup. He is talking about Joseph. About a pit, and twenty pieces of silver, and a lie told to a grieving father. He has understood that this whole strange day is God's hand reaching into a twenty-year-old sin and pulling it into the light. And he does not resist it.

Then comes the most striking part: "We are now my lord's slaves — we ourselves and the one who was found to have the cup." Judah refuses to let Benjamin bear this alone. He ties his own fate to his brother's.

This is a genuinely changed man. And it is worth remembering that from this man's line comes One who would tie Himself to guilty people entirely — not because He shared their sin, but because He chose to carry it (2 Cor 5:21).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you ever recognised God's hand behind circumstances that exposed something in you?
2. What does it look like to stand with someone rather than distance yourself from them?
3. Is there guilt you need to bring into the light today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for uncovering what I could not heal on my own. I bring my guilt into Your light and lay it at the cross, where Jesus has already carried it. Amen.
